title: Rule-Based Pricing Algorithms and Market Outcomes: An Experimental Study
abstract: arXiv:2609.26861v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Rule-based pricing tools are widespread in digital commerce, yet we know little about how their design shapes market outcomes. In a controlled market experiment, participants use dashboards to build pricing algorithms competing in a sequential Bertrand game over multiple periods. We vary design features commonly found in commercial repricing tools: warnings about price wars, pre-configured strategies, and advice from a large language model. Most treatment variations raise market prices with effects driven by an increase in starting prices and more cooperative algorithm designs. The results matter for competition policy, platform regulation and current discussions on regulating algorithm design tools.

translated_title: 基于规则的定价算法与市场结果：一项实验研究
translated_abstract: 基于规则的定价工具在数字商务中广泛使用，但我们对这些工具的设计如何塑造市场结果知之甚少。在一项受控市场实验中，参与者使用操作面板构建定价算法，在持续多轮的序贯伯特兰博弈中进行竞争。我们改变了商业重新定价工具中常见的设计特征：关于价格战的警告、预配置策略，以及来自大语言模型的建议。大多数实验处理都会提高市场价格，其效应源于起始价格的提高和更具合作性的算法设计。这些结果对竞争政策、平台监管以及当前关于监管算法设计工具的讨论具有重要意义。
tldr: 本实验首次揭示，定价算法工具中的常见设计特征（如价格战警告、预配置策略和大语言模型建议）大多会通过提高起始价格并促使算法设计更具合作性，从而推高市场价格，对竞争政策与平台监管具有重要启示。
en_tdlr: An experiment shows that common design features of commercial pricing tools—price war warnings, pre-configured strategies, and LLM advice—generally raise market prices through higher starting prices and more cooperative algorithm designs, with important implications for competition policy and platform regulation.
